title: Energy from Food
notes: Food provides energy for everything our bodies do — running, reading, and even sleeping, when we still need energy to breathe and keep our heart beating. The **energy value** of a food is the amount of energy a certain quantity of it provides. It is shown on **nutrition labels** in **kilocalories (kcal)** or **kilojoules (kJ)**. For example, a snack labelled 100 kcal provides 100 × 4.2 = 420 kJ, because 1 kcal = 4.2 kJ.

Living things do not burn their food. Instead, food is broken down gradually inside cells by **respiration**. During respiration, some of the chemical energy stored in food (**glucose**) is converted into other useful forms of energy for body activities. **Oxygen** is usually needed, and **carbon dioxide** and **water** are usually produced. Respiration is a series of controlled chemical reactions, so energy is released a little at a time rather than in one hot burst.

The process is summarised by two equations. The word equation is: food (glucose) + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water. The chemical equation is: C6H12O6 + 6 O2 → 6 CO2 + 6 H2O. Energy is released in the process. Compare this with photosynthesis, which stores energy in food: respiration does the opposite and releases that energy again.

callout: Exam tip: respiration is not breathing. Breathing only moves air in and out of the body, while respiration is the chemical reaction inside every living cell, plant or animal.

questions.prompt: A 50 g serving of food has an energy value of 300 kcal. Using 1 kcal = 4.2 kJ, what is its energy value in kJ?
questions.why: Multiply the energy in kcal by 4.2, so 300 × 4.2 = 1 260 kJ.
questions.wrongWhy: Dividing by 4.2 instead of multiplying gives 71 kJ. Answer: 1 260 kJ.

questions.prompt: Why does respiration release the energy in food gradually, with no flame?

options.text: Because respiration is a series of controlled chemical reactions inside cells.
Because respiration does not really release any energy.
Because respiration only happens when food is burnt.
Because respiration uses light energy from the Sun.

questions.why: Glucose is broken down step by step by controlled reactions in cells, so energy comes out slowly.
questions.wrongWhy: Burning releases all the energy at once with a flame, but respiration is controlled inside cells. Answer: it is a series of controlled chemical reactions inside cells.

questions.why: Respiration takes in glucose and oxygen and gives out carbon dioxide and water.
questions.wrongWhy: The first option is the photosynthesis equation with reactants and products swapped. Answer: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water.

questions.prompt: In which cells does respiration take place?

options.text: Only in cells that receive light
In both plant cells and animal cells

questions.why: Every living cell needs energy, so both plant and animal cells respire.
questions.wrongWhy: Light is needed for photosynthesis, not respiration, which happens in all living cells. Answer: in both plant cells and animal cells.
